subject: POC sequence plan: evaluation milestones, acceptance tests, and blocker log
messages:
From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Sara Lopez <sara.lopez@acme.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 9 May 2027 15:05:00 +0000
Subject: POC sequence plan: evaluation milestones, acceptance tests, and blocker log

Hi Sara / Devin —

Following our demo last week, attached is an updated evaluation matrix and a proposed sequence for the POC milestones. I want to align on acceptance tests and owners so we can lock the close timeline. High-level plan below: 

- Week 0 (today): access & infra validation (staging cluster credentials + network allowlist) — owner: Acme (Devin) / Redwood (Marissa)
- Week 1: ingestion + latency baseline (sample dataset) — acceptance: median 95th-token latency <= 220ms across 1k sample requests
- Week 2: quality evaluation (1000 prompts, MAP eval set) — acceptance: pass-rate >= 88% on key intents (classification + slot extraction)
- Week 3: scale run & cost estimate — acceptance: sustained throughput of 50 req/s with p95 latency SLA

Open/blocker items we need to resolve before Week 1 starts:
1) Staging credentials: Devin, we still need the kube config and a short-lived service account for our infra tests.
2) Log retention: we need 30d of request logs for quality tracing; confirm this meets your security policy.
3) Network egress: your security team requested an allowlist — attached network-config.pdf should outline addresses we need.

I've attached the poc-eval-matrix.xlsx with the detailed acceptance criteria and eval scripts. Please review and confirm owners and any changes to the acceptance thresholds by EOD Wednesday (May 12). If we hit the thresholds, we will move to a short A/B run and prepare a pilot close proposal.

Next checkpoint: propose Tue May 16, 11:00am PDT (I'll send a calendar invite once we confirm).

Thanks —
Karthik Iyer
Sr. Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachments: poc-eval-matrix.xlsx
From: Sara Lopez <sara.lopez@acme.com>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Devin Ramesh <devin@acme.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC sequence plan: evaluation milestones, acceptance tests, and blocker log

Thanks Karthik — this is helpful. Quick answers and clarifications: 

- We can provide a short-lived kube config by EOD Tue (May 11). Devin will share the service account and we can scope network rules to the IP ranges in your PDF.
- Log retention: our security policy allows up to 90d for non-PII telemetry; 30d is fine but we may request a 90d export if we need longer-term regression analysis. Can Redwood provide an automated export hook to S3?
- Acceptance criteria: the latency threshold looks reasonable; for quality evaluation, we have two additional intents (safety-filtering & calibration). Can you add those to the eval matrix and include the exact prompts used? We prefer not to see PII in the test set.

One more ask: can Redwood run an initial smoke test against our dev cluster (non-prod) and share result logs before Week 1? That will help us confirm the network paths and IAM.

We'll confirm owners once Devin shares the kube config. Tentatively we can do Tue May 16 at 11am PDT.

—Sara
Sara Lopez
CTO, Acme Robotics
(sara.lopez@acme.com)

Quick internal update + note for Acme:

- I'm assigning a Redwood infra lead for the smoke test (Jasmin on infra ops) — Jasmin will coordinate with Devin on kube creds.
- We can add safety-filtering and calibration intents to the eval set; I've added placeholder prompts in the matrix and will replace them with sanitized prompts (no PII) by Wed EOD.
- Blocker: our security team flagged the allowlist IP range you provided. They want to run a quick port-probing exercise before adding outbound rules; this pushes our internal provisioning timeline by ~24-36 hours. Estimated access delivery: Wed May 12 by 18:00 UTC.

I've uploaded an updated network-config.pdf with the minimal IP ranges and a step-by-step onboarding checklist for your infra team. Devin — if you can confirm the chosen CIDR range and a test namespace, Jasmin will start the smoke test immediately upon access.

Marissa Cole
Head of Customer Platforms, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

Date: Wed, 12 May 2027 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC sequence plan: evaluation milestones, acceptance tests, and blocker log

Thanks everyone — pulling this into a short action list to keep us tidy ahead of Tue May 16 checkpoint: 

Action items:
- Devin (Acme): provide kube config + short-lived SA, and confirm CIDR/test namespace — due Tue May 11 (in flight)
- Jasmin (Redwood infra): run smoke test against dev cluster, share raw logs and S3 export hook details — due Wed May 12 18:00 UTC
- Marissa (Redwood): finalize sanitized eval prompts and update poc-eval-matrix.xlsx with safety-filtering/calibration intents — due Wed May 12 EOD
- Karthik (Redwood): prepare A/B run plan and cost estimate conditional on acceptance pass; send calendar invite for Tue May 16 11:00am PDT once creds are confirmed — due Thu May 13

Blockers:
- Access delay due to security port-probing (see Marissa) — ETA Wed May 12 18:00 UTC
- If Acme requests 90d log retention, we need to confirm S3 export policy and egress costs before scaling the run.

Next checkpoint: Tue May 16, 2027 — 11:00am PDT (calendar invite pending).

Priyom Das
Solutions Product Manager, Redwood Inference
